methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Nth Cycle is a Growth-stage climate and energy company founded by Megan O'Connor and Chad Vecitis, having raised $60M in equity plus a $1.1B 10-year offtake agreement with Trafigura. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 8 private peers in Climate & Energy (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix) and 1 public comparable.

A peer-median approach is not applicable here. The Climate & Energy sector at Growth stage lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables—the 8 identifiable peers in the broader sector do not yield the minimum three datapoints needed within narrowly filtered cohorts (same stage, similar tier, or adjacent stage). Expanding to an all-sector median would introduce substantial methodological noise given stage and capital intensity heterogeneity across the peer set.

Without a defensible peer-median result, this valuation remains indeterminate from the data supplied. Rigorous triangulation would require either: (1) expansion of the private peer dataset with stage-aligned datapoints, (2) deeper analysis of the public comparable (LNZA) adjusted for stage and leverage differences, or (3) alternative methods (DCF sensitivity around the $1.1B Trafigura offtake, precedent M&A in recycling/battery materials). The offtake structure is material to downside protection but does not directly imply enterprise value absent revenue visibility and margin assumptions.
